groups.title: Compound nounstem foundation and embed meaning
groups.proposal: Build compound nounstems through the existing NNC plus NNC owner. Keep linked, connectiveless, integrated, and conjunctive structures distinct; preserve embed-before-matrix order; let the matrix determine the compound noun class; and derive the embed's modifier role from typed structure rather than a translation or example inventory.
groups.writingJob: Combine two owner-issued NNC Results into one typed compound Source, preserve both morphemic shapes and their boundary, derive the embed's general-use shape including regular Subclass 2-B final-a retention, and let the typed matrix govern the Result class.
groups.readingJob: Show source NNCs, compound structure, embed-before-matrix order, matrix government, Result noun class, general-use embed shape, wide modifier meanings, and Canvas examples as proof rather than admission lists.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the two NNC Results and the compound structure only when more than one structure is genuinely possible. The application derives order, boundaries, embed shape, matrix government, class, and compatible modifier readings.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse canonical NNC capture and the existing compound operation; do not add stem whitelists, example templates, manual boundary, manual final-a, noun-class, or translation controls.

groups.title: Possessor orientation
groups.proposal: Derive whether a possessive compound's possessor belongs to the matrix or embed from its typed Source history. Linked compounds are embed-oriented; an ordinary integrated compound is matrix-oriented; and an integrated compound built from a possessive adjoined predicate may preserve embed orientation. Ask for orientation only when both analyses truly remain possible.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the source possessive relation through compounding, derive the possessor's target from linked versus integrated structure and captured adjoined-predicate history, keep matrix government distinct from possessor orientation, and retain nested reference identity.
groups.readingJob: Show possessor source, matrix or embed target, linked versus integrated consequences, matrix government, nested ownership, unimportant ambiguity, and examples without turning body-part or compound identities into route gates.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses possessor orientation only where an integrated typed Source genuinely permits both matrix and embed readings. Linked orientation and uniquely inherited integrated orientation are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse typed possessive Source history and referent identity; do not add witness-compound lists, possessor-copy, matrix-government, or automatic-orientation controls.

groups.title: Matrix authority and translation reversal
groups.proposal: Make the typed matrix, not English word order or dictionary glosses, the compound head. Preserve embed and matrix identities when translation reverses them, reject translation-only structural reanalysis, and retain a genuine matrix-versus-embed choice only for the rare typed Sources that license both compound organizations.
groups.writingJob: Carry the selected embed and matrix roles into the canonical Result, let the matrix govern class and compound identity, preserve source order despite translation reversal, and represent rare reversible Sources as two distinct analyses rather than one collapsed form.
groups.readingJob: Show which constituent is matrix and why, Result identity and class, translation reversal, culturally different classification, rare uncertain examples, reversible analyses, and Canvas evidence without using glosses as grammar authority.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses which Source constituent is matrix only when typed lexical analysis licenses both organizations. The application otherwise derives the head, order, class, boundaries, and structural reading automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Use one conditional matrix-selection Analysis; do not infer structure from English, dictionary lookup, example order, or a lexical route whitelist.

groups.title: Simple embed class examples
groups.proposal: Apply the shared compound rule to open typed tli, in, zero, and tl Subclass 1 embeds, deriving ordinary general-use shape and boundary phonology without making the example list productive authority.
groups.writingJob: Derive each compatible embed's general-use compound shape from its typed noun class and preserve the matrix Source and Result class.
groups.readingJob: Show embed class, source shape, realized compound shape, boundary changes, matrix government, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the two typed NNC Sources; regular shape and class consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add example, noun-class consequence, or allomorph controls.

groups.title: tl Subclass 2 and boundary alternations
groups.proposal: Derive Subclass 2 embed shapes and licensed boundary alternations from typed Source structure, including final-a retention, marked lexical loss, long-vowel glottalization, unexpected lexical variants, and final h to y before a vowel.
groups.writingJob: Apply productive Subclass 2 shape rules, preserve typed lexical exceptions without generalizing them, and retain the fuller Source analysis through phonological realization.
groups.readingJob: Show retained or lost a, long-vowel and glottal evidence, h-to-y boundary realization, negative adverbial embed, unique variants, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies genuinely lexical exceptional analysis only when needed; productive shape follows automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create example-stem gates or manual sound-change controls.

groups.title: Unique compound-only nounstems
groups.proposal: Preserve compound-only nounstems as typed lexical analyses that can fill embed or matrix positions without letting their small Canvas inventory authorize the productive compound route.
groups.writingJob: Carry a typed unique-stem analysis, historical uncertainty, and morphemic boundaries through the shared compound owner.
groups.readingJob: Show unique status, embed or matrix position, uncertain history, related formations, boundaries, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies a genuinely lexical unique-stem analysis when not already known; compounding remains productive and automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Lexical inventory identifies facts but never gates valid compounds.

groups.title: The compound-only ca matrix
groups.proposal: Treat compound-only ca as a genuinely lexical matrix meaning an associated, characterized, or made-of entity, while keeping its productivity open to compatible typed embeds and deriving Result subclass from typed compound analysis.
groups.writingJob: Apply the ca matrix to open typed embeds, preserve uncertain embed meanings as lexical evidence, derive the licensed Result subclass, and distinguish unrelated final-ka stems structurally.
groups.readingJob: Show ca matrix status and meaning, embed contribution, Result subclass, unrelated final-ka contrast, later uses, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a lexical ca-matrix analysis only where the typed Source is ambiguous with an unrelated final-ka stem.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not use the listed ca compounds as a route whitelist or final-ka spelling as sufficient authority.

groups.title: The yō matrix and possessive embeds
groups.proposal: Preserve compound-only yō as a typed matrix for characteristic or abundant quality, and allow its licensed possessive-state nonspecific-possessor embeds without collapsing them with absolutive-embed compounds.
groups.writingJob: Build yō-matrix compounds from typed absolutive or possessive embeds, preserve assimilation and internal possession, and keep related meanings and later specialized uses distinct.
groups.readingJob: Show yō matrix meaning, absolutive versus tla-possessive embed history, internal possession, assimilation, related readings, special uses, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses absolutive versus possessive embed history only where both typed analyses survive.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer history from translation or authorize it from the example inventory.

groups.title: Conjunctive compounds
groups.proposal: Build conjunctive compound nounstems as equal conjunct plus conjunct Sources, preserving the first NNC's tl or tli vestige and their possible possessive-state split into separate conjoined NNCs.
groups.writingJob: Keep conjunction distinct from embed-matrix government, derive the first-conjunct vestige, preserve Result class and possessive continuation, and allow later double-nucleus structure.
groups.readingJob: Show equal conjunct roles, retained vestige, Result shape, possessive breakup, double-nucleus relation, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses conjunctive structure only where it competes with a genuine governed-compound analysis.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse conjunction and compound owners; do not add vestige, example, or breakup controls.

groups.title: Recursive compound embeds
groups.proposal: Allow a complete owner-issued compound NNC Result to fill the embed subposition recursively, preserving its internal hierarchy, class, possession, and boundaries.
groups.writingJob: Recapture a completed compound as embed, enforce acyclic nesting, and preserve both inner and outer matrix relations.
groups.readingJob: Show recursive hierarchy, inner compound, outer matrix, boundaries, Result class, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user selects the completed embed Result and outer matrix; hierarchy is automatic when unique.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add depth, example-template, or boundary controls.

groups.title: Recursive matrices and bracketing ambiguity
groups.proposal: Allow compound Results as matrix or in both subpositions and preserve genuine alternative bracketings as distinct typed analyses.
groups.writingJob: Recapture recursive matrix Results, derive the outer Result class from the outer matrix, enforce acyclic structure, and request bracketing only for real ambiguity.
groups.readingJob: Show inner and outer matrices, complete hierarchy, Result class, alternative bracketings, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses bracketing only where the same typed constituents support more than one hierarchy.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not collapse recursive structure by surface spelling or add depth controls.

groups.title: Sex-distinction compounds
groups.proposal: Let typed male or female NNC Results modify compatible animate matrices when sex distinction is intended, without building an animate-stem whitelist.
groups.writingJob: Attach the selected sex-denoting embed to a typed animate matrix and preserve matrix class and referent identity.
groups.readingJob: Show sex distinction, animate matrix, otherwise neutral human reading, matrix class, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses whether to specify sex and the compatible sex-denoting embed; form follows automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not gate the route by the listed animal or human stems.

groups.title: Progeny and fellowship compounds
groups.proposal: Build progeny compounds with typed conē or pil-tōn matrices and fellowship compounds with possessive poh matrices, preserving the different matrix meanings, possession, participants, and lexical restrictions without stem-route whitelists.
groups.writingJob: Apply typed progeny or fellowship matrix analysis, preserve recursive animal descriptions and possessive participant links, and derive ordinary NNC inflection.
groups.readingJob: Show progeny or peer relation, matrix identity, human conē nuance, possession, subject and possessor participants, plurality, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended lexical matrix and participant relation when not already typed; ordinary form is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Keep genuinely lexical matrix meanings typed but do not gate compatible embeds by the example lists.

groups.title: Affinity reduplication scope
groups.proposal: Derive plural affinity reduplication on the embed, matrix, or both from typed compound analysis, preserving obligatory versus optional lexical facts and asking for scope only where more than one realization is genuinely licensed.
groups.writingJob: Apply affinity shape at the licensed Source boundary, preserve vowel length and subject-number structure, and carry optional or obligatory scope as typed analysis.
groups.readingJob: Show plural subject, reduplication target, long-vowel affinity shape, optional or obligatory status, possessive cases, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses affinity target only where typed analysis licenses multiple targets; unique or obligatory scope is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse nounstem reduplication and number owners; do not add example, vowel-length, or obligatoriness controls.

groups.title: Distributive and varietal reduplication
groups.proposal: Apply compound distributive or varietal reduplication to the embed boundary and keep it distinct from matrix affinity reduplication.
groups.writingJob: Derive embed-targeted distributive or varietal shape, preserve glottal and vowel evidence, and retain the full compound Source.
groups.readingJob: Show distribution or variety meaning, embed target, contrast with affinity matrix reduplication, boundaries, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses distributive versus varietal meaning only where context does not decide; target and form are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add target, example, or sound controls; reuse the shared reduplication owner.
